extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and standards governing Board decisions, reopening prosecution after Board action, withdrawal/dismissal of appeals, petitions under 37 CFR 1.198, RCE practice, and judicial review (appeals/civil actions) including timing and service requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action after Board affirmance-in-part with reversal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the decision of the Board is an affirmance in part and includes a reversal of a rejection that brings certain claims up for action on the merits, the examiner will take up the application or reexamination proceeding for appropriate action on the matters thus brought up. However, the application or reexamination proceeding is not considered open to further prosecution except as to such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner acts only on matters brought up by the reversal; other aspects remain closed to prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.196(b) — new rejection procedure when appellant does not act
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Board makes a new rejection under 37 CFR 1.196(b) and no action is taken with reference thereto by appellant within 2 months, the examiner should proceed in the manner indicated in paragraphs I-III of this section (see MPEP §1214.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant fails to act within two months, examiner follows the pre-specified procedures (MPEP §1214.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elect to proceed before examiner after Board 1.196(b) new rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant elects to proceed before the examiner with regard to the new rejection, the Board’s affirmance will be treated as nonfinal, and no request for rehearing of the affirmance need be filed at that time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution before examiner on the 1.196(b) rejection can incidentally overcome the affirmed rejection even though the affirmed rejection is not open to further prosecution. If the application becomes allowed or abandoned it should not be returned to the Board. If the 1.196(b) rejection is not overcome, the applicant may file a second appeal limited to the 1.196(b) rejection (may not include the affirmed rejection). If prosecution of claims rejected under 1.196(b) is terminated before the examiner, the file must be returned to the Board so the original affirmance can be made final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request rehearing of 1.196(b) new rejection — timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appellant elects to request rehearing of the new rejection, the request for rehearing of the new rejection and of the affirmance must be filed within 2 months from the date of the Board’s decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 2‑month filing requirement applies to rehearing requests on new rejections and affirmances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal dismissed for failure to argue a ground of rejection covering all appealed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal has been dismissed for failure to argue a ground of rejection involving all the appealed claims, see MPEP §1215.04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissal can occur if the brief fails to argue a ground of rejection involving all appealed claims; see detailed dismissal rules in §1215.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must inspect files returned from the Board and mark allowed claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When a file is received after decision by the Board, it must be examined and appropriate precautions taken to indicate the presence of allowed claims, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the 'Contents' page with notation such as 'Allowed Claims' or 'Rejection Reversed' immediately below the 'Decision by Board' endorsement to avoid overlooking allowed claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.198 — reopening after Board decision (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases decided by the Board will not be reopened or reconsidered by the primary examiner except under the provisions of §1.114 or §1.196 without the written authority of the Commissioner, and then only for the consideration of matters not already adjudicated, sufficient cause being shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reopening by examiner is tightly constrained; written Commissioner authority required except where statutes/regulations allow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment filed after Board decision — RCE required to reopen prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after the Board’s decision which presents a new or amended claim is not entered as a matter of right; however, if the amendment is submitted with a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 and the fee (1.17(e)) the prosecution will be reopened and the amendment entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, or to design applications. See MPEP §706.07(h). An appeal brief or reply is not a submission under 1.114 unless the RCE transmittal expressly incorporates those arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of amendments that obviously put application in condition for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment obviously places an application in condition for allowance, regardless of whether the amendment is filed with an RCE, the primary examiner should recommend that the amendment be admitted, and with the concurrence of the supervisory patent examiner, the amendment will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if prosecution is closed, clearly allowable amendments should be recommended for entry and admitted with supervisory concurrence. Note MPEP §1002.02(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: When amendment cannot be entered — notice and non‑arbitrary refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment cannot be entered, the examiner should write to the appellant indicating that the amendment cannot be entered and stating the reason why. The refusal may not be arbitrary or capricious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 12.19 'Amendment After Board Decision, Entry Refused' and identify new issues in Examiner Note bracket 2. Do not use this form where a 37 CFR 1.196(b) rejection has been made by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass to issue when claims stand allowed after Board decision
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event that claims stand allowed in the application under the conditions set forth in MPEP §1214.06, paragraph II, the application should be passed to issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If allowed claims exist after Board action, process the app to issuance rather than returning to Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision authority for petitions to reopen under 37 CFR 1.198
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.198 to reopen or reconsider prosecution of a case after decision by the Board, where no court action has been filed, are decided by the Technology Center Director (MPEP §1002.02(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner also entertains certain petitions under limited categories (see next rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of petitions ordinarily grantable under 37 CFR 1.198 (Commissioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commissioner will ordinarily grant petitions only in categories: (A) Board decision suggests rejection proper because claims omit a disclosed limitation or suffer a curable defect and decision reasonably suggests claims including the limitation or devoid of defect would be allowable; (B) Board decision asserts record lacks evidence of specified character, and it's reasonably suggestive that presenting such evidence would make claims allowable and such evidence exists and can be offered; (C) Board decision based on practice/rule/law/judicial precedent which since has been rescinded, repealed, or overruled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions ordinarily will not be entertained after filing of Commissioner's brief in 35 U.S.C. 141 cases, or after trial in 35 U.S.C. 145 cases. If petition granted in a 141 appeal, steps taken to request court remand so proposals/amendments/evidence/arguments are entered of record; in 145 cases seek dismissal without prejudice to consideration of proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal — who may withdraw and effect on application
rubrics_metrics.description: Except where withdrawal of an appeal would result in abandonment, an attorney not of record may file a paper under 37 CFR 1.34(a) withdrawing an appeal. Where, after an appeal has been filed and before decision by the Board, an applicant withdraws the appeal after the period for reply to the final rejection has expired, the application is to be considered abandoned as of the date on which the appeal was withdrawn unless there are allowed claims in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter abandoning under 37 CFR 1.138 has effective date of recognition by the Office or different date specified in letter. If a brief has been filed and an answer mailed and appellant withdraws, the application is returned to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE filing before Board decision reopens prosecution and effects on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to a decision by the Board, an applicant wishing to withdraw an application from appeal and reopen prosecution can file an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 accompanied by a responsive submission and the RCE fee. The filing of an RCE will be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal by the applicant, regardless of whether the RCE includes the appropriate fee or a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE practice under 1.114 does not apply to utility/plant apps filed before June 8, 1995, design applications, or reexamination proceedings. When an RCE is filed without the appropriate fee or a submission in an application that has no allowed claims, the application will be considered abandoned. To avoid abandonment, file RCE in compliance with 37 CFR 1.114. An appeal brief or reply is not a submission under 1.114 unless the RCE transmittal letter incorporates by reference the arguments in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify Board when refiling or RCE filed to avoid conflicting decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should promptly inform the clerk of the Board in writing as soon as they have positively decided to refile or to abandon an application containing an appeal awaiting a decision. Applicants also should advise the Board when an RCE is filed in an application containing an appeal awaiting decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to exercise appropriate diligence may result in the Board refusing an otherwise proper request to vacate its decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims when appeal withdrawn/dismissed and some claims allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application contains allowed claims as well as claims on appeal, the withdrawal of the appeal does not operate as an abandonment of the application, but is considered a withdrawal of the appeal as to those claims and authority to the examiner to cancel the same. An amendment canceling the appealed claims is equivalent to a withdrawal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some claims are allowable only by virtue of dependency from rejected claims, they are treated as rejected (see examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial withdrawal vs. cancellation of withdrawn claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawal of the appeal as to some of the claims on appeal operates as an authorization to cancel those claims from the application and the appeal continues as to the remaining claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawn claims will be canceled by examiner at the conclusion of appeal proceedings if necessary (e.g., if examiner is reversed as to remaining claims) without further action by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal of appeal for failure to file brief — consequences and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If no brief is filed within the time prescribed by 37 CFR 1.192, the appeal stands dismissed by operation of the rule. If no claims stand allowed, an application is considered abandoned on the date the brief was due. If claims stand allowed in an application, the failure to file a brief and consequent dismissal of the appeal is to be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal and of any claim not standing allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-461 or form paragraph 12.17 may be used to notify appellant; such notice is not an action and does not start any period for reply. Do not dismiss until the extended period (5 months under 37 CFR 1.136(a)) to file the brief has expired. If formal matters remain, examiner should set a shortened period for reply and the application is closed to further prosecution except as to such matters (form paragraph 12.09.01, see MPEP §1206). Appeal also dismissed if applicant fails to timely and fully reply to a notice of noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.192(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies after dismissal — petitions to revive and reinstatement of canceled claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal is dismissed and allowed claims remain, the application is not abandoned; to reinstate claims canceled by examiner because of the dismissal, the applicant must petition to reinstate the claims and the appeal, but a showing equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper reply to the notice of noncompliance must be filed before the petition will be considered on its merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of examiner handling based on allowed/rejected/dependent claim status
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative handling: (A) Claim 1 allowed; claims 2 and 3 rejected — cancel 2 and 3 and issue with claim 1 only. (B) Claims 1-3 rejected — hold application abandoned. (C) Claim 1 rejected and claim 2 objected as allowable except for dependency — hold abandoned. (D) Claim 1 rejected and claim 2 objected (dependency); independent claim 3 allowed — cancel claims 1 and 2 and issue with claim 3 only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These examples show correct examiner responses to mixed claim statuses after appeal/ dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review options and waiver consequences (35 U.S.C. 141 vs 145)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with the decision in an appeal to the Board may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141). By filing such an appeal the applicant waives his or her right to proceed under section 145 (civil action in District Court). A patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding may appeal and seek court review under 35 U.S.C. 141-145 as provided (subject to statutory changes and filing-date limitations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of judicial route has waiver implications; check applicability based on filing dates and type of proceeding (ex parte vs inter partes).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.301 — steps for appeal to U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant or patent owner dissatisfied with the Board may appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit. The appellant must file in the PTO a written notice of appeal directed to the Commissioner (see §§1.302 and 1.304); and in the Court, file a copy of the notice and pay the fee as provided by the rules of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inter partes reexamination proceedings filed under §1.913, §1.983 is controlling.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.303 — availability of civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145/146/306 (date-limited applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant or patent owner involved in certain reexamination proceedings for patents that issue from original applications filed before November 29, 1999, may, instead of appealing to the Federal Circuit, have remedy by civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 or 146. For ex parte reexamination proceedings for patents issued from originals filed on/after November 29, 1999, no remedy by civil action under 145 is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an appeal to the Federal Circuit waives the right to proceed under 35 U.S.C. 145. Procedural distinctions depend on filing dates and whether proceeding is inter partes or ex parte.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.304 — time for filing notice of appeal or commencing civil action (two‑month rule and tolling)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing the notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit or for commencing a civil action is two months from the date of the Board's decision. If a request for rehearing or reconsideration is filed within the time provided, the time for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action expires two months after action on the request. In interferences the time for filing a cross-appeal or cross-action expires 14 days after service of the notice of appeal or summons and complaint, or two months after the date of decision, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These periods are not subject to 37 CFR 1.136, 1.550(c), 1.956, or 1.645(a) or (b). Times are calendar days/months; add one day to any two‑month period including February 28. If last day falls on weekend/federal holiday in D.C., extend to next non-weekend/non-holiday. Commissioner may extend time for good cause (if requested before expiration) or for excusable neglect (if requested after expiration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing cross-appeal or cross-action — specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.304(a) specifies the time for filing a cross-appeal or cross-action expires (A) 14 days after service of the notice of appeal or the summons and complaint; or (B) two months after the decision to be reviewed, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The district court will determine whether any cross-action was timely filed since neither the complaint nor cross-action is filed in the PTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time standard for initiating judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner may extend the time for filing an appeal or commencing a civil action for good cause if requested in writing before the expiration of the period, or upon written request after expiration upon a showing that the failure to act was the result of excusable neglect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is similar to the Federal courts. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(b), 1.136(a) fee extensions and 1.550(c) are not available once the last decision has been entered. Requests should be addressed to the Commissioner (Box 8) Attention: Office of The Solicitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of court papers on the Commissioner / Office of the Solicitor
rubrics_metrics.description: All service copies of papers filed in court proceedings in which the Commissioner is a party must be served on the Solicitor of the Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service may be by hand between 8:30 A.M. and 5:00 P.M. EST at the Office of the Solicitor, or by mail to: Office of the Solicitor, P.O. Box 15667, Arlington, VA 22215. Hand-carried deliveries are allowed. Do not supplement the above mail address to refer to the Commissioner or the USPTO. Any court papers mailed elsewhere are deemed served when actually received in the Office of the Solicitor. The mail service address should not be used for filing a notice of appeal to the Federal Circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative file confidentiality during judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative file of an application under judicial review, even though carried to a court, will not be opened to the public by the USPTO, unless it is otherwise available to the public under 37 CFR 1.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During judicial review, the involved application or reexamination is not under the jurisdiction of the examiner or the Board unless remanded to the USPTO by the court.
